coverage: Weekend edition, week of Nov 9 to 13, preview of Nov 16 to 20
moodReason: Stocks rallied broadly and semiconductors jumped about 8%, but a hot CPI report pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to about 5.14% and markets treat a December Fed hike as close to certain.

stories.headline: Hot October CPI drives Treasury yields and Fed hike bets higher
stories.what: October CPI rose 0.4% month over month against 0.3% expected, and core rose 0.3% against 0.2%, a third straight upside surprise. The 2-year yield jumped about 17 basis points on Tuesday and the 10-year finished the week near 5.14%, its biggest weekly rise since April 2025.
stories.why: Higher yields raise borrowing costs and cut the present value of future earnings, which hits richly priced growth stocks hardest. The 10-year auction on Tuesday drew the weakest demand since June.

stories.headline: Fed officials open the door to a bigger December hike
stories.what: Governor Waller backed a 25 basis point hike in December and said a 50 basis point move could be considered. Dallas Fed President Logan called for at least two more hikes, and Hammack favors smaller, more frequent moves. Fed funds futures now treat a December quarter-point hike as near certain, with about a 12% chance of a half-point move.
stories.why: A series of hikes would tighten financial conditions further, and the debate over the size of the move adds uncertainty for stocks and bonds alike. The Fed decides on Dec 8 to 9.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang pushed out after China-linked report
stories.what: Jensen Huang was pushed out as Nvidia chief executive on Thursday after reports linked him to an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore chip buyer suspected of routing chips to China. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while an outside search begins. The stock opened about 13% lower, fell as much as 14%, and closed down just over 4%.
stories.why: Nvidia is the bellwether for AI chip demand, so leadership uncertainty and China-linked chip questions weigh on the whole AI trade. The stock has now fallen six weeks in a row, its longest losing streak since 2012, ahead of its Nov 17 earnings report.

stories.headline: Stocks rebound with semiconductors and energy leading
stories.what: The S&P 500 gained 2.5% to 7,561.67, the Dow rose 2.1% to 52,353.24 and the Nasdaq rose 2.3% to 25,136.27. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index gained about 8% and all 11 sectors finished higher. The VIX fell 24.7% on the week to 19.30.
stories.why: The rebound shows buyers returning after the early-November selloff, but the rally is narrower than the headline suggests. The S&P 500 is still about 3.3% below its Oct 6 record, the Nasdaq is about 9% below its record, and roughly 55% of S&P 500 stocks remain in long-term downtrends.

stories.headline: Dollar strengthens and the yen nears 160 per dollar
stories.what: The dollar index rose about 1.1% on the week to roughly 103.4, its best week in two months. USD/JPY climbed above 160, raising intervention concerns in Japan.
stories.why: A stronger dollar trims overseas earnings for US multinationals and tightens conditions for emerging markets. Possible Japanese intervention could also move global bond yields quickly.

stories.headline: Oil slips for a second week as Iran talks stall
stories.what: Brent dipped below $90 on Tuesday for the first time since August, then rebounded to near $96 by Friday, and finished the week down about 2.5% at $95.84. WTI fell 1.6% to $88.91. Crude rose more than 3% intraday on Thursday after President Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran. The EIA expects a supply surplus to build in 2027.
stories.why: Lower oil eases inflation pressure, but Iran headlines keep a geopolitical premium in prices. The EIA's surplus forecast points to lower energy prices next year if it holds.

stories.headline: Bitcoin breaks below $70,000 and gold falls under $4,000
stories.what: Bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time since August, ending the week near $68,000 after a sixth straight weekly decline, with more than $1 billion in leveraged positions liquidated in a single day. Gold dropped below $4,000 after the CPI report, closing near $3,884, its lowest level in about a year.
stories.why: Higher real yields reduce the appeal of non-yielding assets like gold and bitcoin, and leveraged selling amplifies the moves. Crypto weakness can also spill into speculative tech names.

Monthly options expiration, a possible source of volatility
FOMC decision, where a December rate hike is now widely expected

bottomLine: Stocks had a strong week led by chips, but the S&P 500 is still about 3.3% below its October record and market breadth remains weak. The bond market delivered the opposite message: a hot CPI report pushed the 10-year yield to about 5.14% and made a December Fed hike look almost certain. Nvidia's leadership shake-up makes its Nov 17 earnings report the week's key test for the AI trade, and the rate outlook will decide whether this rebound holds.
